wwo.name: Genoa
wwo.method: The circa 1894 Meyers city panel supplies related street axes, port basins, blocks, open ground and hachured slopes. The 1899 Baedeker consultation and archival records constrain use for the 1900 opening date. Parcel dimensions and heights are inferred within mapped blocks. The northern approach follows the Darsena quay, Via Pre and Via Balbi toward Carmine and the hillside belt. The seaward approach follows the old harbour and Sarzano through Carignano toward the historic mouth of the Bisagno. The lower Bisagno opens into the printed sea and continues north through the Porta Pila crossing. The west-side record separates the Meyers harbor front from the stable natural shore recorded in the 1884 port survey. Via Balbi connects to a mapped uphill lane where the blocks give way to hachures.

registration.model: Least-squares affine from the 1280 by 983 Meyers reproduction to WGS84. Period structures were matched to surviving metric point references. City-center point references within large features are approximate.

controls.name: Albergo dei Poveri central court group

registration.limitation: Control fit measures consistency at recognized places. Printed building blocks and projected controls do not establish individual facade locations. The western quay and lower river are extrapolations.

sources.precision: Meyers Konversationslexikon, fifth edition, volume 7, 1:13,300 city panel. Digitized from 1280 px faithful reproduction. Printed scale bar gives about 3 m per source pixel. Positional uncertainty also includes generalization and registration.

sources.precision: Only the natural coast and dry foreshore west of Lanterna are used. The circa 1894 Meyers regional inset supports the continuity of the pre-expansion coast at broad scale. The chart gives no individual opening-date building or quay at Sampierdarena.

limitations: Landforms are preserved as mapped constraints. The current elevation input cannot recover the subsequently excavated San Benigno hill.
Shore and open river traces are generalized. The old quay structures and pre-1905 harbor footprint remain provisional at close range.
The 1899 works near Porta Pila and Brignole and later twentieth-century coastal additions remain outside inferred blocks.
No individual building is asserted from the small printed marks. The period streets and basin edges remain candidates for runtime inspection.
The 1894 map does not supply dated elevation or sufficient surveyed position for close building placement. The 1899 reproduction was consulted only.
The western overlap includes only the reported natural foreshore and the range of the original historic sheets. Sampierdarena and Albaro remain incomplete.

The lower Bisagno remains open through the old Porta Pila bridge. The paired-bank record stops at the next documented bridge. Upstream bank geometry, period woodland and the pre-excavation San Benigno surface remain unresolved.

west_shore_registration.method: Local similarity from the 1280×865 historical chart into the 1280×983 Meyers sample frame, then the established affine. The two prints depict the same promontory and the existing outer port before the twentieth-century expansion.

controls.feature: Molo Vecchio beacon at the seaward end

west_shore_registration.limits: The 1884 chart supports coastal shape and predecessor shore position. The coarse 1894 inset corroborates continuity. It cannot independently locate a bank from 1900, measure intervening fill, or recover the excavated San Benigno terrain.

A bounded part of the printed rail approach. Track and land width are diagrammatic.
Ground behind the printed dry quay edge, enclosing the Dogana and Arsenal area. The dark quay perimeter and Darsena Reale basin define its seaward edge.

Two readable banks from the mouth through the old Porta Pila bridge, continuing to the upstream railway crossing. The remaining visible sliver upstream has one bank cropped by the Meyers sheet. The rail crossing marks the limit of the paired-bank reach in this record.
